_comment: Provenance for WASM bundles built from the pqctoday-hsm repo and vendored into this hub. When you rebuild a bundle with its hsm build script, update its `hsmCommit`/`builtAt`. Verify drift with `npm run sync:wasm:check` (compares against a sibling ../pqctoday-hsm checkout when present; no-op otherwise). Bundles built from other sources (openssl upstream, pqctoday-tpm) are intentionally omitted.

bundles.name: cacp-kmip
bundles._buildNote: Rebuilt 2026-08-02 from hsm main @ 8386717 (v0.20.2) via scripts/build-kmip-wasm.sh with HUB= pointed at the remediation worktree (the script stages straight into a sibling pqctoday-hub by default — override it or it writes into whatever branch the main checkout happens to be on). Closes a 2-commit drift (v0.17.0 9f618c4 + v0.16.0 4f08746). The script's own node smoke test passed end-to-end in wasm, including a real hybrid-KEM encapsulate/decapsulate round-trip. Scope note from the 2026-08-02 audit: the v0.17.0 PKCS#11 fixes in this window are NOT reachable through any KMIP operation — the ECDH cofactor gate lives in the C-ABI dispatch layer while kmip/src/ops/derive_key.rs calls native::ecdh_agree() directly (no mechanism parameter at all), KMIP has no sign-recover concept, and ECDH-as-KEM is C++-engine-only. So this rebuild is provenance hygiene, not a behavior fix. Prior entry (cfd71fc, 2026-07-25): follow-up rebuild closing a 1-commit drift the CSD02 migration's own last hsm commit (cfd71fc, KAT provenance metadata) introduced against the prior entry (8e7b09c/2026-07-24) — found by running the provenance check with an explicit HSM_REPO_PATH override before shipping this release, since the default sibling-path check is a no-op without one. cfd71fc only touches kmip/kat/*.json documentation (no wasm-exported function signatures, no engine behavior), so this rebuild is a formality for the release record, not a functional change — confirmed via another real `cargo build --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` + `wasm-bindgen` + live node smoke test (Query, Create, malformed-frame handling, ML-DSA-65 CreateKeyPair/Sign/SignatureVerify round-trip, an unimplemented-algorithm rejection, and a full X25519MLKEM768 hybrid-KEM CreateKeyPair→Activate→Encapsulate→Decapsulate round-trip — not simulated), from a clean worktree exactly matching `hsmCommit`. `sync:wasm:check:cacp-kmip --check` is clean after.

bundles.name: softhsmrustv3-engine
bundles._buildNote: Rebuilt 2026-08-02 from hsm main @ 8386717 (v0.20.2), closing a 26-commit drift found by running this repo's own `sync:wasm:check` during a PKCS#11/HSM playground gap audit. Built with rust/build-wasm-bundle.sh (wasm-pack --target bundler --release -- --features acvp, 8MB shadow stack, __wbg_get_memory shim re-applied automatically by the script). Copied byte-identically to all three vendored locations (public/wasm/rust/, src/wasm/, src/vendor/softhsm-wasm/wasm/) — verified matching md5 d284c8f1ca61c53b9152ee2dff80ce1b. Pulls in, among 26 commits: the C_Login TOCTOU race fix (099ca25), PKCS#11 token-scoping isolation enforcement on native::* (a2c2b64), the cross-tenant isolation panic when Ed25519 isn't selected (e27b40a), CK_RSA_PKCS_OAEP_PARAMS native-width parsing (0335131 — native-only, no wasm32 behavior change), RSA sign/verify-with-recovery C_SignRecover/C_VerifyRecover (eed556e, PKCS#11 v3.2 §5.13), the CKM_ECDH1_COFACTOR_DERIVE-vs-CKK_EC_MONTGOMERY rejection (6270b73), SLH-DSA bench-harness completion (d97d669 — harness-side only; all 12 FIPS 205 param sets were already dispatchable in the engine before this window, so the playground's '12 parameter sets' claim was never false), and the v0.20.2 Dependabot cmov+rand Cargo.lock patches. VERIFIED: export surface is unchanged vs the prior bundle (.d.ts export-list diff empty); vitest src/components/Playground/hsm + keystore 141/141 pass against this binary; full `npm run test:local` shows the identical 6 pre-existing failures as the un-rebuilt baseline across two consecutive runs (no new failures; one transient opTemplates pollution flake did not reproduce and passes 27/27 in isolation). NOTE: the wrapper files src/wasm/softhsm.ts and src/wasm/softhsm/loaders.ts previously hardcoded _C_SignRecover*/_C_VerifyRecover* to CKR_NOT_IMPL, masking the engine implementation this rebuild ships — fixed in the same change. Prior entry (5c0eadd, 2026-07-17): PKCS#11 v3.2 Baseline Provider + generic pre-hash mechanisms (hsm commit 644a839, landed directly on main): adds the CKO_PROFILE object (CKA_PROFILE_ID=CKP_BASELINE_PROVIDER, every Profiles v3.2 §5.1 requirement checked against the fetched spec) and implements the previously-unadvertised generic CKM_HASH_ML_DSA (0x1F) / CKM_HASH_SLH_DSA (0x34) pre-hash mechanisms (CK_HASH_SIGN_ADDITIONAL_CONTEXT.hash parsing, remapped onto the existing hash-specific mechanisms). `hsmCommit` above (5c0eadd) is a same-day follow-up that only refreshes hsm's own tracked rust/pkg_bundler/ build artifact + a wasm/Cargo.lock version bump — no rust/ source changed beyond 644a839. No new exported wasm functions — same API surface (.d.ts/.js text diffs are empty), only the .wasm binary changed; verified 302 Rust unit tests pass (0 failed) and the .wasm binaries are byte-identical across all three hub vendor copies (public/wasm/rust/, src/wasm/, src/vendor/softhsm-wasm/wasm/ — the last of which was found stale relative to the other two, predating the FrodoKEM/McEliece shadow-stack fix, and is now back in sync as a side effect of this rebuild). Prior entry (`5303bd3`, 2026-07-11): fixed the FrodoKEM/Classic-McEliece wasm32 shadow-stack overflow in Encapsulate — see hsm CHANGELOG.md for that history.

bundles.name: softhsm-cpp-engine
bundles._buildNote: Rebuilt 2026-08-02 from hsm main @ 8386717 (v0.20.2) via scripts/build-wasm.sh, closing a 5-commit drift. Pulls in ECDH-as-KEM under C_EncapsulateKey/C_DecapsulateKey (a450d42), the CKM_ECDH1_COFACTOR_DERIVE-vs-CKK_EC_MONTGOMERY rejection (6270b73), the v0.19.0 emsdk 6.0.4 / OpenSSL 3.6.3 toolchain fixes (e85b26d), and the Split Key secret-sharing math (4cc4c4b). Built with emsdk 6.0.4 — NOTE for future sessions: emsdk was already installed at /Users/pqctoday/Antigravity/emsdk and only needed `source emsdk_env.sh`; a prior audit wrongly recorded emcc as unavailable on this machine because `emsdk install --build=source` is invalid syntax and its failure was read as 'no toolchain'. Verified with the repo's own tests/smoke-wasm.mjs against this exact binary: C_Initialize through C_Finalize, ML-KEM-768 C_EncapsulateKey/C_DecapsulateKey producing matching 32-byte shared secrets. Staged to all four hub copies: public/wasm/softhsm.{js,wasm}, public/wasm/libsofthsmv3.{js,wasm} (the raw cmake output names) and src/vendor/softhsm-wasm/wasm/softhsm.{js,wasm}; all three .wasm copies are byte-identical (md5 c6890a8414bd486df5f37776f891f2d1) and softhsm.js is libsofthsmv3.js with the wasm filename patched, exactly as build-wasm.sh does it. Prior entry (e912488d, 2026-06-27): includes fix(cpp) 250994d — SP800-108 KDF now requires keyed-MAC PRF (CKM_SHA256_HMAC); bare hash IDs rejected per PKCS#11 v3.2 §6.42.

bundles.name: openssl-pkcs11
bundles._buildNote: PKCS#11 engine swapped from the C++ SoftHSMv3 fork to the pure-Rust softhsmrustv3 (hsm rust/, wasm32-unknown-emscripten staticlib). The C++ fork's only crypto backend is OpenSSL libcrypto -- the same libcrypto.a linked into this binary -- so the chain CLI -> pkcs11-provider -> C++ softhsm -> same libcrypto was circular. The Rust engine has no OpenSSL dependency (RustCrypto + patched fips204/205/ml-kem), making the provider path a genuinely independent implementation. Build flags: -sSTACK_SIZE=8MB (Emscripten's 64KB default overflows during ML-DSA/ML-KEM keygen and traps with 'memory access out of bounds'). pkcs11-provider config.h is now generated by scripts/gen-pkcs11-provider-config-h.sh rather than required to pre-exist, and defines DEFAULT_PKCS11_MODULE so the provider resolves the in-process engine with no config file. The apps_startup() provider-registration patch ('Fix A') is recovered into pqctoday-priv/openssl-wasm-patches/ after previously existing only inside a gitignored openssl source tree -- verified at parity with the shipped binary before this rebuild. Token-state persistence across openssl.wasm's per-command modules (-sEXIT_RUNTIME=1) uses a NEW mechanism: a genuine C atexit() hook (registered in this hub's own src/wasm/cms_provider_init.c) calls a new Rust export, pqctoday_hsm_atexit_stash, which writes engine state to a fixed MEMFS path; JS reads it back via a pure FS.readFile after callMain returns. This replaced an earlier design that assumed OpenSSL's own provider teardown (C_Finalize) would run during callMain's atexit chain -- verified directly that it does not: OPENSSL_cleanup() runs on every callMain but never unloads a provider loaded via an explicit OSSL_PROVIDER_load() call, which is how this embedding registers pkcs11. ML-KEM keys now carry CKA_ENCAPSULATE/CKA_DECAPSULATE per PKCS#11 v3.2 SS6.68.2 (previously CKA_DERIVE, which is wrong for KEM keys). Token-init decisions now query the token's own CKF_TOKEN_INITIALIZED flag (C_GetTokenInfo, newly exported) rather than inferring from JS-side bookkeeping alone, per PKCS#11 v3.2 SS5.5.7. Verified end-to-end in Node against this exact binary: provider loads reporting the Rust engine; C_InitToken/InitPIN/GenerateKeyPair(ML-DSA-65 and ML-KEM-768) succeed; a real ML-KEM-768 encapsulate/decapsulate round trip across a fresh module produces byte-identical shared secrets; a 4-step CMS workshop flow (keygen -> self-signed cert -> cms sign -> cms verify), each step in its OWN fresh module, round-trips a real payload correctly using only the file-based snapshot handoff. Pinned anchor KATs (ML-DSA-44/65/87, SLH-DSA-SHA2-128s, ML-KEM-512/768/1024 decap, bit-flip negatives) pass against this binary. NOT YET VERIFIED: a full pass in an actual browser (all proof above is Node-against-the-binary); a possible second lost OpenSSL source patch referenced by the build script's own banner comment ('HRR detection') has not been confirmed present or absent.
